answers: 네, 아스피린 알레르기가 있어요. (네, 아스피린에 알레르기가 있어요.)
Three times a day, 30 minutes after each meal.

dialogue.meaning: Welcome. What brings you in? (Where does it hurt?)
I have a headache and a fever.

dialogue.korean: 그럼 이 감기약 드세요. 하루 세 번, 식후 30분에 드세요.
dialogue.meaning: Then take this cold medicine. Take it three times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

exercises: Choose the right word to finish the sentence: 콧물이 ( 아파요 / 나요 ).
Choose the right word to finish the sentence: 머리가 ( 아파요 / 나요 ).
The pharmacist asks: '처방전 있으세요?' You don't have one. Answer in Korean.
The pharmacist asks: '언제부터 아프셨어요?' You started feeling sick this morning (오늘 아침). Answer in Korean.
The pharmacist asks: '알레르기 있으세요?' You are allergic to aspirin (아스피린). Answer in Korean.
The pharmacist says: '하루 세 번, 식후 30분에 드세요.' In English, how many times a day should you take the medicine, and when?
objective: By the end, learners can buy an over-the-counter medicine at a Korean pharmacy: say one symptom with '머리가 아파요 / 콧물이 나요 / 열이 나요', answer the pharmacist's questions (처방전 있으세요? 언제부터요? 알레르기 있으세요?), and understand the dosing instruction '하루 세 번, 식후 30분에 드세요'.
setting: A small neighborhood pharmacy (동네 약국) in Korea on a weekday evening. The customer has a cold but did not go to a doctor, so they have no prescription. They talk to the pharmacist at the counter.
summary: A short, realistic conversation at a Korean pharmacy. A customer without a prescription describes a headache, fever and runny nose, answers the pharmacist's questions, and gets instructions for taking cold medicine.
